related_questions.question: What does a US citizen need to enter South Africa?

text_blocks.snippet: US citizens generally don't need a visa for stays of 90 days or less in South Africa for tourism or business purposes. However, they do need a valid passport with at least 30 days of validity remaining beyond their planned departure date, and two blank pages for entry and exit stamps.
snippet_highlighted_words: a valid passport with at least 30 days of validity remaining beyond their planned departure date, and two blank pages for entry and exit stamps

text_blocks.snippet: Requirements for US citizens entering South Africa:

list.title: Passport:
list.snippet: A valid U.S. passport is required, with at least 30 days of validity remaining after your planned departure date.

list.title: Blank Passport Pages:
list.snippet: Your passport must have at least two blank pages (labeled "Visa") for entry and exit stamps.

list.title: Visa:
list.snippet: If your stay is longer than 90 days, or for purposes other than tourism or business (e.g., work or study), you will need to apply for the relevant visa before traveling.

list.title: Return or Onward Ticket:
list.snippet: You may need to show proof of a return or onward ticket.

list.title: Sufficient Funds:
list.snippet: You may need to demonstrate that you have sufficient funds to support yourself during your stay.

list.title: Yellow Fever Certificate:
list.snippet: If you are arriving from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission, you may need to provide proof of yellow fever vaccination, according to Friendly Planet Travel.

list.title: Children:
list.snippet: If traveling with children under 18, you may need to show an unabridged (full) birth certificate in English, according to Yellow Zebra Safaris.
